title: Is Restrictive Eating Behavior in Anorexia Nervosa Short-sighted? An Experimental Investigation
official: Is Restrictive Eating Behavior in Anorexia Nervosa Short-sighted? An Experimental Investigation
summary: The investigators will examine the behavioral effects of an experimental Episodic Future Thinking manipulation on food choice, as well as the ability to engage the neural circuits supporting Episodic Future Thinking during food choice, among individuals with anorexia nervosa (AN) and healthy controls.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria

Individuals with Anorexia Nervosa:

1. DSM-5 diagnosis of AN
2. Right-handed
3. Hospitalized as an inpatient at New York State Psychiatric Institute
4. Able to provide informed consent

Healthy controls:

1. Right-handed
2. BMI ≥ 18.5 and ≤ 25 kg/m2
3. No history of eating disorder or other psychiatric illness
4. Not currently dieting
5. Able to provide informed consent

Exclusion Criteria

Individuals with Anorexia Nervosa:

1. Current or lifetime history of DSM-5 schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, or other psychotic-spectrum disorder
2. High risk of suicide
3. Food allergy that would interfere with study participation
4. Daily psychotropic medications within 1 month of the study
5. Major neurological problem that might affect interpretation of findings
6. Indwelling metallic object (e.g. braces, non-removable metal jewelry, medicinal patch or recent metallic ink tattoo)
7. Significant claustrophobia
8. Pregnancy

Healthy controls:

1. Any current or lifetime eating disorder
2. Any current psychiatric disorder
3. Current psychotropic medication
4. Food allergy that would interfere with study participation
5. Major medical or neurological problem that might affect interpretation of findings
6. Indwelling metallic object (e.g. braces, non-removable metal jewelry, medicinal patch or recent metallic ink tattoo)
7. Significant claustrophobia
8. Pregnancy
